claims.claim: AI scale-up and scale-out architectures increase the need for high-bandwidth, power-efficient optical connectivity; Lumentum's laser and InP capacity therefore sits on a physical connectivity bottleneck rather than merely an application-layer AI theme.

The NVIDIA purchase commitment plus Lumentum's planned 240,000-square-foot Greensboro InP facility create a demand-to-capacity causal chain, but the mid-2028 production ramp leaves a long execution interval in which architectures, yields or supplier share can change.

FY2026 operating evidence strengthens scenario robustness: revenue reached $3.014B, up 83.2% year over year, with GAAP operating margin 17.4%, showing the optical thesis is already converting before the new fab ramp.

claims.claim: The core AI-optics thesis is not falsified by current operating evidence: FY2026 revenue and operating margin expanded sharply and management guided to further Q1 FY2027 growth.

Reported FY2026 GAAP net loss is not evidence of operating collapse: it was dominated by a one-time non-cash $7.8B loss on extinguishment associated with equitization of convertible notes; this nevertheless makes capital-structure/dilution effects a material red-team item.

The strongest present falsifier is execution/concentration rather than demand absence: committed demand and new capacity can still disappoint if customer architecture, supplier allocation, fab schedule or yields change before mid-2028.
